subject: design-technology
title: Foundations of CAD/CAM
welcome_lead: Boot up your workstation and learn what CAD and CAM really mean for modern designers.
meta_desc: Learn the basics of CAD, CAM and common software for GCSE Design & Technology.
final_note: You can name CAD packages, explain how CAM links to them and list key benefits.

concepts.def: Computer-aided design — drawing on a computer.
Computer-aided manufacture — machines that cut or print.
Flat drawings used for laser or vinyl cutting.
Solid models with depth, used for 3D printing.
Language CAM machines read to move tools.
Photo-realistic image generated from a 3D model.

walkthroughs.body_html: CAD replaces pencil and paper with software like SolidWorks, Fusion 360, TinkerCAD or Inkscape. It allows accurate measurements, easy edits, 3D rotation and photo-realistic renders to show clients before anything is made.
The CAD file is exported (often as .STL or .DXF) and passed to CAM software. The CAM program creates G-code that tells a CNC router, laser cutter or 3D printer exactly how to move and at what speed.

A designer sketches a keyring in Inkscape (2D CAD), exports a DXF and loads it into the laser cutter software. The CAM software generates a cut path and the machine cuts identical keyrings in acrylic in under a minute each.
